chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: Al-Khadr ibn Muslim al-Sayrafi narrated that I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Three [types of people] will be under the Shade of the Throne of God, the Exalted and Mighty, on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade: A man who judged people fairly regarding himself; a man who did not hasten to do something nor delay it until he knew that was for God's, the Exalted and Mighty, pleasure or displeasure; and a man who did not find fault with his brother with a fault until he removed that fault from himself, for indeed he does not remove a fault from himself except that another fault replaces it, and sufficient is the man's occupation with himself rather than with people.

key_terms.أَنْصَفَ النَّاسَ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: Who judged people fairly regarding himself
key_terms.ظِلِّ عَرْشِ اللَّهِ: Shade of the Throne of God
key_terms.لَمْ يُعَيِّبْ أَخَاهُ: Did not find fault with his brother
key_terms.يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ: The Day when there is no shade except His

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that lead to being under the Shade of God's Throne?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three traits as essential for divine proximity, emphasizing that true piety begins with internal self-accountability before external judgment. The third characteristic specifically warns against the hypocrisy of criticizing others while ignoring one's own flaws, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on *muhasaba* (self-examination). This hadith serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate sincerity (*ikhlas*) and humility in their daily interactions.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-4 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Al-Khazr ibn Muslim al-Sayrafi, “I heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say

‘Three groups of people will be under the Shade of the Honorable the Exalted God on the Day in which there is no shade other than God’s Shade. The first group are those who treat the people fairly. The second group are those who only do what pleases God, and do not do anything which would raise God’s Wrath. The third group of people are those who do not express the faults of their Muslim brothers in their absence, unless they first remove such faults from themselves. It is better to attend to the improvement of one’s own faults than to seek out other people’s faults.’”
